definitions.explanation: Something that conclusively determines an outcome. Originally from sports (a decisive hit or play), now widely used figuratively for the final factor that settles a matter.

examples.japanese: {決定打|けっていだ}に{欠|か}ける{試合|しあい}だった。
examples.english: It was a match that lacked a decisive blow.

examples.japanese: この{問題|もんだい}にはまだ{決定打|けっていだ}となる{解決策|かいけつさく}がない。
examples.english: There is still no conclusive solution to this problem.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{証言|しょうげん}が{裁判|さいばん}の{決定打|けっていだ}になった。
examples.english: His testimony became the decisive factor in the trial.

notes: A compound of {決定|けってい} (decision/determination) + {打|だ} (hit/blow). Very commonly used in the negative pattern {決定打|けっていだ}に{欠|か}ける (to lack a decisive blow), meaning the situation remains unresolved. Common collocations: {決定打|けっていだ}を{放|はな}つ (to deliver a decisive blow), {決定打|けっていだ}になる (to become the clincher), {決定打|けっていだ}がない (there is no decisive factor).
